hints.text: $270^\circ$ is three quarter-turns, landing at the bottom of the circle.
The bottom point of the unit circle is $(0, -1)$, and sine reads the $y$-coordinate.

explanation: Three quarter-turns counterclockwise put you on the negative $y$-axis, at the very bottom of the circle.
On the unit circle that point is $(0, -1)$.
Sine is the $y$-coordinate, so $\sin 270^\circ = -1$ — the lowest value sine ever takes.

alternativeExplanations.title: A Ferris wheel picture
steps: Imagine riding a Ferris wheel of radius 1 centered on the origin, starting at the right side.
After three quarters of a turn you are at the very bottom, one unit BELOW center.
Below center means a height of $-1$, so $\sin 270^\circ = -1$.
